correctness.rationale: All \(2^{14}=16384\) states are included. For any flippable spin with \(r=2\) or \(3\) disagreeing neighbors, the disagreement-edge count changes by \(3-2r=-1\) or \(-3\), so the backward absorption equations are acyclic and exact. check_cyclic.py uses cyclic Fano lines and increasing-edge-cut dynamic programming; check_xor.py uses \(\mathbf F_2^3\) incidence lines and a separately implemented recursive rational Bellman solver. Both run successfully and return the same 15 Bernstein coefficients, identical q-polynomial and 56 three-spin cases. The \(1/15\) success probability has a direct \(3/6\) times \(2/5\) times \(1/3\) local race proof. Finite exhaustive proof is valid for the fixed 14-site domain, with no claim of infinite extension.

value.rationale: The Heawood Fano graph is the smallest cubic girth-six graph, providing a canonical sparse-network metastability benchmark. The complete rational absorption polynomial resolves a natural probability for all initial spin densities, while rare nucleation is characterized by Fano noncollinearity and a 1/15 bridge race. The known synchronous protocol has the same 56 mixed fixed states but isolated basins; at unbiased spins its mixed fixed-state probability is 7/2048, compared with the asynchronous 0.283824, a substantial and motivated kinetic contrast. Exact finite value does not require an unproved extension to larger graphs.
